newsitem.title: USA: Applied Magnetics calls off Read-Rite bid.
newsitem.headline: Applied Magnetics calls off Read-Rite bid.

text.p: Applied Magnetics Corp., whose stock plunged after it said it wanted to acquire rival Read-Rite Corp. for $1.8 billion, said Friday it was withdrawing its hostile bid because of the stock decline.

"Although we continue to believe the strategic rationale for this combination is compelling, we recognise that based on the current value of Applied Magnetics' common stock the transaction is not feasible," Chief Executive Craig Crisman said in a statement.
Read-Rite responded that it is "pleased" with the move.

"We are pleased that they have withdrawn their offer, and are particularly pleased with the tremendous support we have received from shareholders, customers and employees," a Read-Rite spokesman said.

Applied Magnetics' stock, after being temporarily halted after the announcement, tumbled as low as $29.25 before ending $2 lower Friday at $31.375 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most heavily traded issues.
Less than a month ago, the stock traded at $60.50 -- before the company, a maker of disk drive components, announced its hostile bid for Read-Rite, which makes similar computer components.
Read-Rite rejected the Feb. 24 bid, saying a combination with Applied would interfere with its strategy for the future.
That set off a sharp decline in the stock of Applied Magnetics, which had planned to use its stock to pay for the acquisition, as well as that of Read-Rite.
When Applied Magnetics announced its offer to swap 0.679 Applied share for each Read-Rite share, the bid was based on an Applied Magnetics share price of $55.25 as of the Feb. 21 market close.

Analysts generally agreed with Read-Rite's defence, which argued that Applied was pursuing it to make up for weaknesses in its production capacity and technological progress toward the next generation of disk-drive head technology.
